correctness.rationale: For every n, solving the site update for its leftmost input gives a bijection between cyclic predecessors and fixed points of a product of two sixteen-state maps. Exact complete finite closure has 491 transformations, rank four for every four-letter product, two primitive 240-element classes, and ten transversal four-point images per kernel class each with 24 bijections. Consequently no rank-four transformation can have three fixed points; small n are exhaustively checked. A free S4 relabeling of the four kernel blocks commutes with transition maps, forcing uniform stationary fiber permutations. Irreducible aperiodic finite chains give exponential convergence, and S4 fixed-point counts 9,8,6,1 give the claimed law. The included checker re-computes all finite premises and independent same-period fibers up to n12; a finite experiment alone is not used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: This is a natural dynamical invariant for a specifically published intermediate-degree locally eventually onto nonlinear cellular automaton. Its infinite-map inverse degree is four, but a random periodic output has zero same-period predecessors 3/8 of the time and 5/8 are reachable, quantified by a complete 0/1/2/4 law. The exact contrast between infinite and cyclic fiber structures, no-three boundary, and finite-sheet monodromy has independent mathematical interest, and does not follow from textbook surjectivity or routine point counting.
